meta.title: El Salvador Mining History: Pre-Colonial to 2024 Reversal

summary.brief: El Salvador's mining history features artisanal gold extraction from the early 20th century, industrial operations in the 1970s-1990s by U.S. firms like Commerce Group, severe environmental pollution, social violence including 2009 activist murders, a landmark 2017 metal mining ban, and its reversal in December 2024 under President Bukele amid economic promises.
keyTakeaways: San Sebastián Gold Mine produced approximately 35 metric tons of gold from 1904-1953.
2009 murders of anti-mining activists Marcelo Rivera, Ramiro Rivera, and pregnant Dora Sorto in Cabañas department.
El Salvador became the first country to ban all metal mining in 2017; reversed Dec 23, 2024.
Legacy pollution: arsenic levels in San Sebastián River 300 times WHO limits; economic contribution historically <1% GDP.

content.text: There is limited evidence of organized mining in pre-colonial El Salvador. Significant gold mining activity began during the colonial era with artisanal operations, but systematic extraction traced to the early 20th century. Colonial references note gold in regions like Cabañas, but no large-scale production documented.

Artisanal gold mining commenced around 1904 at San Sebastián Gold Mine (La Unión department), operated initially by Butters Salvador Mining. By 1953, it yielded ~35 metric tons of gold. Santa Elena mine produced ~32 tons from 1904-1954.

U.S.-based Commerce Group Corp. industrialized San Sebastián in the 1970s, making it economically significant. Operations paused during civil war (1980-1992), resumed post-peace accords until 2006 permit revocation due to pollution.

Post-1992, ARENA government issued 28 exploration licenses to foreign firms (U.S., Canada, Australia). Pacific Rim Mining (Canada, later OceanaGold) acquired El Dorado mine (Cabañas) in 2002 for proposed industrial development.

points.text: 2008-2009: Heightened tensions in Cabañas amid Pacific Rim opposition; 6 murders including anti-mining activists.
Jun 2009: Marcelo Rivera Moreno (environmentalist) kidnapped, tortured, murdered.
Dec 2009: Ramiro Rivera Gomez murdered; Dora Alicia Recinos Sorto (8 months pregnant) and son shot.

content.text: Activists linked violence to pro-mining interests; Pacific Rim denied involvement. Sparked national/international outcry.
San Sebastián River contaminated by cyanide, arsenic, mercury from Commerce Group operations; ongoing acid drainage turns water red.

content.title: Pollution Levels in San Sebastián River

content.text: Health impacts: cancer, respiratory issues; 90% surface water polluted nationally.

points.text: Commerce Group/San Sebastián Gold Mines v. El Salvador: ICSID dismissed 2011.
Pacific Rim v. El Salvador (CAFTA/ICSID): $250M claim dismissed 2016; firm ordered to pay El Salvador $8M costs.

content.text: After grassroots campaigns (National Roundtable Against Metallic Mining, CRIPDES, Radio Victoria, Catholic Church), FMLN govt enacted worldwide-first total ban on metal mining.
Dec 23, 2024: Bukele's New Ideas party (57/60 seats) overturns ban; state monopoly on mining, bans mercury use. Claims vast reserves ($3T gold); critics cite pollution risks.
Economic context: Mining historically ~0.3% GDP; recent GDP from mining ~$31M Q1 2025.
